clue.text: Father, saint or priest

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
ST is the standard abbreviation for saint
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of the kinds of churchman one might address: a father, a saint or a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make it look like a list of definitions, but only the last word defines; the rest is spelt out piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister in charge of a congregation, a kind of clergyman like a priest.

clue.text: "Choose love", declared Spanish fighter

indicators.note: something declared is said out loud, so the answer follows the spoken words

parts.note: to choose is to pick, and to love is to adore

explanation.surface: A Spanish combatant romantically announces that he picks love over war.
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is the mounted man with a lance in a Spanish bullfight.

clue.text: Suspect has disturbed day after quiet start

indicators.note: things disturbed are moved out of their usual order
after sends the piece it follows in the clue to the back, so the word before it goes second

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
the letters of day rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal suspect has had a troubled day after a calm beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a noun for an accused person; it is the adjective meaning dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady means of doubtful honesty, so it serves as an adjective for questionable dealings.

clue.text: Utter two unfavourable decisions

wordplay.note: an umpire's out ruling is bad news for a batsman, and two of them joined by and

explanation.surface: Someone is told to voice a pair of rulings that went against them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like a verb meaning say; it is the adjective meaning total. In cricket an umpire gives a batsman out, a decision against him.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means complete or thorough, as in an out-and-out lie, matching utter as an intensifier.

clue.text: Late time for cricket?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: arriving after the expected time
second, playful meaning: the moment when another set of six balls is due to be bowled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the cricket is running behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls; read as two words, the answer says one of them is due, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has not arrived by its expected time, so it is behind schedule.

clue.text: Organ starting very loud kills church services

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, the only one kept

parts.note: first letter of Organ
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
to ice someone is slang for killing them

explanation.surface: An organ opening at full volume ruins the worship.
explanation.definitionFit: The daily offices are the set forms of prayer in church liturgy, such as matins and evensong.

clue.text: Finished going topless and became more relaxed

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, and going without it removes that letter

parts.note: to have ceased is to have finished

explanation.surface: Someone stopped wearing a top and loosened up as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to lessen in tension or become less strained, so eased means loosened up.

clue.text: Lay assistance backed up one's analysis

indicators.note: in a down entry, backing up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or song
aid means help or assistance
one is I, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: Non-professional help supported someone's study of a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like an adjective meaning amateur; it is the old noun for a ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is the identification of a problem through examination, a form of analysis.

clue.text: Lay out pilot officers drowned in river

indicators.note: something drowned sinks beneath water, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
PO is the RAF abbreviation for pilot officer, plural POs

explanation.surface: Airmen are laid out after drowning in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose is to uncover and leave open to view, to lay bare.

clue.text: Imagined a great deal in daytime

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: DT is a short form of daytime
reams means a great deal, a large quantity

explanation.surface: Someone did a lot of daydreaming during working hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamt is a past tense of dream, which can mean to fancy or picture something in the mind.

clue.text: Series of disasters brought to book?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for a run of mishaps one after another
second, playful meaning: mishaps written up as one section of a volume

explanation.surface: A string of calamities ends with someone held to account for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought to book' normally means made to answer for wrongdoing; here it is taken literally, the mishaps gathered into a section of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an unlucky sequence of mishaps, each following another as if scripted.

clue.text: Frank character

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to mark a letter as paid for postage
second meaning: kind or sort, as in a man of that type

explanation.surface: Someone is described as an outspoken, honest personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like an adjective (honest) or a name; it is the verb for marking post.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp a letter is to frank it, and a stamp is also a distinctive kind or quality.

clue.text: Senior academic takes in the elderly

indicators.note: to take in a guest is to house them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
ye is an old-fashioned spelling of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

explanation.surface: An older university lecturer offers a home to aged people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senior academic' looks like one phrase, but only 'Senior' defines; 'the elderly' means the word the in its antique form.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most senior or respected member of a group, so the word serves as a noun for its eldest figure.

clue.text: See 9
Fellow feeling hidden danger heading off to coastal town

indicators.note: with its head gone, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a trap is a concealed danger
a port is a town on the coast with a harbour

explanation.surface: A sense of comradeship is threatened by an unseen peril on the way to the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, sympathetic understanding between people, a mutual sympathy.

clue.text: Margin apt to be distorted in flyer

indicators.note: distorted things are twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A page's border is likely to be warped in a printed leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a leaflet; it means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountain and Arctic regions, a bird and so a flyer.

clue.text: Vegetable drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gourd such as butternut
second meaning: a fruit cordial diluted with water

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a vegetable juice; in Britain squash is the everyday name for a fruit concentrate topped up with water.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash names both the gourd family vegetable and the diluted fruit cordial.

clue.text: Pants, possibly, in the course of sport

parts.note: under can mean during or in the course of, as in under construction
to sport something is to wear it

explanation.surface: Someone's trousers come up during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants means underpants, not trousers; 'possibly' marks it as one example. 'Sport' is a verb, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Underpants are one example of the garments worn beneath clothes.

clue.text: Arrest queen in strapless bodice

parts.note: to halt is to stop or arrest
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: Royalty is detained wearing a revealing top.
explanation.walkthrough: A halter top has no shoulder straps, being held up instead by a band behind the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter is a backless top fastened by a band around the neck, without shoulder straps.

clue.text: Under Casanova, vice accumulates rapidly

parts.note: Casanova was a famous rake, a womaniser
a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: Following a famous seducer's example, wickedness spreads fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' places the second piece below the first, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake in money is to earn it quickly and in large amounts.

clue.text: Crack regiment traps extremists in Delhi street

indicators.note: something that traps holds a thing caught inside it

parts.note: the SAS, Special Air Service, is a British crack regiment

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: first and last letters of Delhi
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: An elite army unit catches militants in a road in India's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack regiment' reads as one phrase; 'Crack' does double duty as a verb hint, sadists being those who crack the whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadists enjoy inflicting pain, the sort to crack a whip over victims; the definition is a loose, playful one.

clue.text: Charm foreign nobleman in place of bishop

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat or diocese
duc is French for duke

explanation.surface: An overseas aristocrat wins people over, standing in for a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In place of' looks like substitution; it is in plus the bishop's place.
explanation.definitionFit: To seduce is to lure or entice, so it means to charm someone into something.

clue.text: Magic, like a cup-holder, you might say

indicators.note: you might say marks the answer as matching the sound of a spoken phrase

parts.note: a saucer holds a cup, so something like one is jokily saucer-y

explanation.surface: A conjuring trick is compared to the plate under a teacup.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is the use of supernatural powers, witchcraft or wizardry.

clue.text: Throws out carbon in European planes

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for European

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: jets are aircraft
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Carbon is expelled from European aircraft engines.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject is to expel forcibly, to throw someone or something out.

clue.text: Completely full agreement heard following fix

parts.note: a jam is a fix, a tight spot

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the spelling follows the sound rather than the word

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: A total accord is reported after a deal is struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like a verb meaning settle; it is a noun for a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Jam-packed means crammed to capacity, an informal intensive for crowded.

clue.text: Sound car needs a spot of oil

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car

indicators.note: a spot is a tiny amount, so just one letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of oil

explanation.surface: A car in good condition just requires a little oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound car' reads as a roadworthy vehicle; sound is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio means recorded or transmitted sound, as on a soundtrack.

clue.text: In literature, curates keep popping up

indicators.note: in here means contained within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Clergymen are forever appearing in novels and plays.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of literature and the start of curates.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again and again, reappearing repeatedly over time.

clue.text: I''m included in revolutionary strike

indicators.note: something included in another is placed within it

parts.note: Che Guevara is the standard crossword revolutionary
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A speaker announces they have joined a radical walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests reversal, but it is the noun, a revolutionary figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock or bell chimes when it strikes the hour.

clue.text: Criminal leader looked older behind bars

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of Criminal
to have aged is to have grown or looked older

explanation.surface: A gang boss has visibly aged during his time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Something caged is locked in by bars, like a prisoner in a cell.

clue.text: Arcane vertices redrawn round base

indicators.note: a redrawn figure has its parts set down afresh in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle: the corners of a mysterious shape are sketched again around its bottom edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' joins the added letter to the anagram fodder; base is the mathematical constant, not the bottom of a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something hidden or kept mysterious, so arcane works as a loose synonym.

clue.text: Time of day when students return to Irish county

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way one came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the NUS is the National Union of Students
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: The hour when undergraduates head home to Ireland for the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundown is the evening moment when the sun sets, so it names a point in the day.

clue.text: Jaunty American character transported back by British railway

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for British

indicators.note: something transported is carried inside a vehicle, so it sits within the other piece

parts.note: RY is an abbreviation for railway

indicators.note: going back means reading the letters from end to start

parts.note: Americans call the letter Z zee

explanation.surface: A cheerful Yank is carried home on a British train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British railway' looks like BR; it is split into two abbreviations, with the reversed letter name riding inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Breezy describes a lively, carefree manner, a synonym of jaunty.
